name: scene-feedback-harness
description: Review reference images and reconstructed scenes, annotate visual errors, and deliver image feedback through MCP tools and events.

defaultPrompt: 进入人工调试模式，让我在参考图和当前场景上指出问题。
Review this reconstruction with annotated visual feedback.
interface.longDescription: Compare reference images with reconstructed 3D scenes, mark visual errors, and share original and annotated evidence through a project-specific MCP service. Use the folder icon beside Scenes to browse service-host directories or paste an absolute path. Open and import discovers ready instances recursively within scan limits, adds them without switching the current editing scene, and does not create a Codex task. Imported scenes in blank/Events services initially use event delivery. Select a scene and open Tasks to explicitly connect a same-user Codex Desktop task on the service host or create a conversation for that scene, using the single local Desktop connection without a seed binding. Successful connection saves direct delivery for future feedback, preserves event origins and history, and survives restart and unload/reimport. Existing events are not replayed or forwarded to the new conversation, and new feedback is not delivered twice. Images, cameras, marks and drafts remain; other scenes stay unchanged. The blank homepage is only an entry and cannot bind its own conversation. Repeated sources and request retries reuse scenes, individual failures report reasons and continue, and original GLBs, Blender files and references stay intact with separate workbench data and feedback. Imported and created scenes can be unloaded from their list rows with inline confirmation, including unavailable scenes; the default scene is protected. Unloading the current scene saves its prompt draft and returns to the default scene. The unloaded state persists across restarts, while source files, workbench data, feedback and Codex tasks remain. Running work, unresolved delivery checks and in-flight operations block unloading with a specific reason. Reimporting the same source restores the original project, session and edited result without creating a task or replacing it with the initial model. Type @ in one prompt to reference the currently selected object or part and this round’s unsent annotations. A sidebar scene-reference button inserts another loaded, available scene from the same workbench as 🏞️1 without changing the current task binding or modifying the source. Frozen scene JSON and complete GLB copies, with available model preview and first GT image, remain usable after the source updates or unloads. Model previews are generated in the background; confirmed unchanged snapshots can reuse their preview across rounds and reloads. If preview generation fails, available GT can serve as the reference; without either, an error is reported and the reference is not added. Model summaries include only the reference name, version and archive path plus preview/GT evidence; full geometry is read on demand. Up to four scenes per feedback with GLB copy budgets of 200 MiB per scene and 400 MiB per feedback. References stay within this service, and @ candidates are unchanged. The native prompt input and chat history display icons with stable numbers: object 🧊1, part 🧩1, mark 📍1, image 🖼️1, human evidence 🧍1, correction ✏️1, time 🕒1 and scene reference 🏞️1. Rounded source cards provide full names, exact source details and removal. Each kind has independent numbering, repeated sources reuse their number, and existing drafts migrate automatically while preserving exact source bindings. Archived data retains protocol tokens and precise source metadata. Item-level references display as 🧊 object and part-level references as 🧩 part while preserving exact node tokens; both reference types for the same node can coexist. A red outline follows the selected target’s shape: item mode outlines the whole selected group, part mode only the selected target, and the outline follows view and animation changes. Click a source card or inserted reference icon in the prompt to open a small nearby popover with source details or original and annotated image previews. Hover alone does not open it; leaving both the reference and popover closes it automatically. It has no modal backdrop or background dimming and does not take input focus. Touch and keyboard users can dismiss it with the close button, Escape or a click outside. Source labels above the prompt stay clickable, and native drag selection, IME and undo remain available. Invalid mark references retain their icon, number and original name; source cards label them deleted or invalid. Sending lists affected references and locates them in the prompt so the reference can be removed or the mark deletion undone. Double-click an item or part in live 3D, an object-list row or the selected name to insert its exact reference. Single clicks still select; orbiting and dragging do not cite. Double-click a mark-list entry or a visible mark in selection-arrow mode on either image to cite it. Mark-list single clicks wait briefly before showing the source; keyboard activation shows it immediately. Press F to focus the selected target. Double-click the progress thumb, reference frame counter or a saved screenshot time to cite that precise source. Pending thumb citations wait for their target frame and are canceled by a subsequent seek or source change. Successful or waiting double-click time citations show no notification; actual failures still report an error. Type / to cite exact moments or spans from the current clip and this round’s evidence, or double-click the current timeline time to cite the actual clock; Enter or Space also works when the time has keyboard focus. The prompt uses short time references such as 🕒1; clickable cards show precise times, views and reference frames, and sending restores the complete exact description. Repeating the same source and moment reuses its number, while different times stay separate and draft reloads preserve bindings. Editing times are expressed in the prompt. Drag images or use evidence buttons to add other visual references. The scene view keeps one row of compact cards below the image: interactive 3D first, followed by frozen screenshots in capture order. Cards smoothly expand in place on mouse hover or visible keyboard focus; touchscreens keep compact cards for direct taps. Annotation tools adapt to blank space around each pane’s visible image: horizontally above or vertically on the right. If both fit, the roomier side is used; without suitable blank space, the toolbar overlays the top. Placement updates with window size, zoom, pan, split/immersive layout and screenshot changes, and stays steady during drawing, panning or an open tool menu. Hovering the upper area, right-side blank space or toolbar opens the tools; the top of the image remains an entry point, with touch and visible keyboard-focus access. Moving into the tools or More menu keeps them open; leaving the entry area and tools closes them after a short delay while preserving the selected tool and ongoing gestures. The left reference image offers Intelligent contour (Livewire): click anchors to follow image edges with a moving preview, click the first to close, or use Enter/double-click for an open path. Backspace removes the last anchor; Escape cancels, and changing reference, frame, tool or session discards unfinished work. Finished contours are ordinary freehand marks for undo, erasing, references and feedback; add anchors along weak edges. Switch camera views with reference thumbnails while keeping the current clip time. The glass conversation panel starts at 480px wide on desktop and expands to 760px on hover, keyboard focus or touch tap, enlarging only the input area and existing evidence. History opens manually and stays closed after the panel automatically shrinks and expands again. Evidence and details fold temporarily while saved size, position and drafts remain intact. After the pointer leaves and typing stops, it shrinks and closes mention, time and attachment menus; lingering focus, completed selections and idle menus do not hold it open. Active typing including IME composition, keyboard navigation, touch editing, dragging and pending answers keep it expanded, while input, references and Send remain available. It can be moved by dragging its header background, with per-session position preferences and a reset gesture. Custom positions may extend partway beyond the sides or bottom, with limited overflow at the top so the header remains reachable to drag it back. Reloading, expanding, shrinking and viewport changes retain the saved position preference while keeping the header accessible. Overlay opacity and ground direction are directly available in the scene toolbar; reference camera alignment sits between the two views in comparison mode and above the scene in immersive mode. Frozen screenshots support cursor-centered wheel zoom from 0.1× to 8× (minimum 10%) and panning by dragging empty space in Select mode, Space with left drag, or middle/right drag. Each screenshot saves its own viewing position across switching and draft reloads. Images, overlays and marks transform together while original pixels, fixed cameras and normalized mark coordinates stay unchanged; viewing zoom is not sent. Live 3D keeps its existing wheel controls. Drawing on live 3D automatically freezes the current view and completes the same gesture on its screenshot. Further marks stay on that image; returning to 3D and drawing again creates another screenshot while retaining earlier evidence. The workbench supports multiple camera views, dynamic frames, imported WholeBody133 evidence and manual hand keypoint corrections. Human reconstruction and tracking run in a separate capsule skill. Feedback delivery selects relevant cited and marked sources and needed current views, omits empty annotation copies and identical images, and keeps complete evidence archived. MCP feedback returns compact summaries by default; workspace_get_feedback can return full archived fields on request. Open and import automatically checks each candidate model, reference, camera and frame time. Invalid instances report errors while valid instances continue importing; model-only packages and missing cameras show importable warnings for manual comparison. The bundled workbench-ready-check skill lets agents check sources before handoff with the read-only command-line checker, which provides compact or JSON reports without creating workbench data or a model task. These checks do not reopen Blender or establish reconstruction or alignment quality. Experimental MCP Events delivery requires a supporting host and a verified subscription.
